extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, chymists, and learned readers interested in experimental philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological criteria for assessing claims and experiments in chymistry (mixtion, elementhood, and chemical analysis) as argued in a philosophical/experimental treatise. Focuses on what counts as evidence that a substance is elemental or that a mixture truly contains separable ingredients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward bold chymical assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be impos'd upon by hard Names, or bold Assertions; nor be dazzl'd by that Light which should but assist us to discern things the more clearly. 'Tis one thing to be able to help Nature to produce things, and another thing to Understand well the Nature of the things produc'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat artisan confidence as insufficient: claims from 'skilful artists' should not be credited merely because practitioners perform operations. Anti-pattern: accepting authoritative or ostentatious statements about substances' natures without independent scrutiny or reasoned examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate production from understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Being able to make or produce something by art (help Nature) is distinct from understanding what the produced thing really is (its true nature or constituent principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explanatory evidence, not just successful manufacture. Example: many can beget children yet be ignorant of internal parts; likewise a chymist's skill in producing a substance doesn't prove knowledge of its elemental composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent experimental verification required
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who hear claims should, where possible, examine the experiments themselves; curiosity without skill or opportunity is not sufficient, but confidence in assertions should be tempered by the need for trial and replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require reproducibility and opportunity for others to try the same procedures. Anti-pattern: general learned public accepting assertions because they have read about a performance rather than reproduced it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality claims about number of elements must be proven across bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not prov'd by Chymists that three is precisely and universally the number of the distinct substances or elements into which mixt Bodies are resoluble by the Fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generalize from a subset of analyses; test many kinds of compound bodies. A valid universal claim must be supported by evidence that all types of mixt bodies resolve into that specific number (neither more nor less).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recoverability (separability by analysis) as evidence of ingredient retention
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 'Miscibilia' or ingredients of a mixt Body may be again separated by chymical resolutions (fire, menstruums), that manifests that they retain their forms in the compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separations (e.g., aqua fortis dissolves silver leaving gold) as diagnostic evidence that constituent ingredients preserved their nature. Example: quartation — aqua fortis dissolving silver and leaving gold as powder shows retention; anti-pattern: claiming elemental identity when the supposed ingredient cannot be recovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion and active qualities as diagnostic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion or behaviour of a mixt Body follows the nature of the predominant element; many things show that elementary qualities remain active in mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observable dynamical properties (e.g., gravitational tendency toward the centre for earth-dominated bodies) as indicators that elemental forms or qualities persist in a mixture. This is an auxiliary line of evidence complementing chemical separations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for clustering, texture, and proportion effects on separability
rubrics_metrics.description: The ease with which ingredients are separable depends on the minute clusters/coalitions of particles, their cohesion, and the proportions in which ingredients are mixed; some clusters retain their nature and are separable, others cohere so strictly as to form new, inseparable Concretions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate experiments with attention to proportions and texture: small differences (e.g., amount of elixir mixed with lead) can change whether separation by fire or menstruum succeeds. Anti-pattern: treating all mixtures as uniform or ignoring proportion/texture dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid begging the question in definitions of 'mixtion'
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions that assume the conclusion (e.g., defining mistion so that every minute part must contain all elements) should not be used to dismiss opposing evidence; do not define mixture so narrowly that empirical counterexamples are precluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing theories of mixture, use definitions compatible with empirical testing (juxta-position vs perfect union). Example contrasts: Aristotelian 'every minute part contains all elements' vs ancient/chymical juxta-position where ingredients remain separable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider non-fire formative principles and alternative generation hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Some objections note that plants/animals fashion new bodies by a plastick or seminal principle (not by fire); one must consider whether observed substances in living bodies are products of such formative powers rather than simple rearrangement by heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between substances produced by vital/plastic principles and those arising from heat/chemical operations. Do not automatically generalize from biological generation to thermal analysis; consider plausible alternative mechanisms and design experiments that isolate causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming elemental (uncompounded) status requires further negative evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Substances obtained by chymical analysis and called 'Principles' or 'Elements' are not thereby proved uncompounded; one must test whether they can themselves be further decomposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve calling a substance 'elemental' until attempts to decompose it (by known analyses) fail; treat assertions of primitiveness cautiously. Example: the Chymists' 'Tria Prima' may themselves be compounds and require examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of counterexamples from natural processes to challenge dogma
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations that salt and sulphur (or oil and spirit) can be produced from mere water by the plastic power of plants challenge the dogma that certain bodies are primogeneal principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and weigh natural experimental counterexamples against universal doctrinal claims. Empirical demonstrations from varied natural sources serve to undermine blanket assertions (e.g., that salt and sulphur are primary and uncreateable).
